included: A completed experiment that did not improve its target metric.
A completed experiment whose aggregate improvement hides a material regression or error-cancellation effect.
A repeated technical failure only when it invalidates the experiment's optimization or evaluation signal.
excluded: One-off command, path, dependency, authentication, or network errors.
Experiments that have not run or are waiting for external results.
A development-only regression that was subsequently resolved by positive held-out evidence.

metric_definitions.question_score_mae: Mean absolute score error over 70 student-question pairs: 7 development students times 10 questions.
metric_definitions.question_exact_agreement: Fraction of the 70 student-question pairs whose predicted score exactly equals the official score.
metric_definitions.severe_error_rate_abs_ge_5: Fraction of the 70 student-question pairs with an absolute score error of at least 5 points.
metric_definitions.total_score_mae: Mean absolute error between predicted and official total score over 7 development students.
metric_definitions.item_absolute_error_points: Sum of absolute errors over all 70 student-question pairs.
metric_definitions.student_total_absolute_error_points: Sum of absolute total-score errors over all 7 students.
metric_definitions.within_student_cancellation_gap: Item absolute error points minus student total absolute error points. A larger gap means over-scores and under-scores cancel more when question scores are summed.

physics_skillopt_r4.summary: The optimizer merged an under-score and an over-score into one stricter edit. Validation hard accuracy fell from 0.25 to 0.00 and soft exact-subquestion accuracy fell from 0.7917 to 0.4792. One candidate validation output also failed after consuming the full completion budget.

dsaa3071_candidate_v31_r2.interpretation: The apparent total-score improvement is entirely explained by increased cancellation between question-level over-scores and under-scores while question-level absolute error worsened.

design_confounds: C32 changes the rubric, prompt, and skill together.
Only Q7, Q8, Q9 and the top-level grading policy changed between rubric v1 and rubric v2; Q5 and Q6 rubrics did not change.
Each condition was evaluated once and the recorded target temperature is null, so target-model variation was not estimated.

verified_findings: C3 is worse than R1 on question MAE, exact agreement, and severe-error rate.
Q7 contributes all 14 net additional item-level absolute error points in C3 versus R1 before gains and losses on other questions offset one another.
C31-r2's better total-score MAE coexists with 22 more item-level absolute error points and 34 more cancellation points than R1.
C32 reduces item-level absolute error by only 4 points while reducing student total absolute error by 40 points; 36 of the 40 points come from additional within-student cancellation.
C32 adds 19 item-level absolute error points on Q6 while removing 15 on Q5 and 5 on Q9.
C32 has one more severe-error pair than R1.
limitations: The split contains only seven development students.
Official per-question scores are available, but official per-question rationales are not.
Behavioral explanations based on model evidence and flags are diagnostic hypotheses, not verified explanations of the official scores.
C32 is a joint package change, not a single-factor ablation.
